posts.title: A Complete Docker Setup for Laravel in Two Files: Dockerfile and compose.yaml
posts.summary: The full Dockerfile and compose.yaml for a Laravel project with PHP, Nginx, MySQL, a queue worker and the scheduler, plus the commands to start, deploy, back up and manage everything from those two files.
posts.content:
Most Docker tutorials for Laravel end with a folder full of config files that nobody on the team fully understands. It does not need to be that way. A complete stack, with PHP, Nginx, MySQL, a queue worker and the scheduler, fits in two files that live in your project root: a Dockerfile and a compose.yaml.

This article gives you both files in full, explains every part, and then shows how to run the whole project day to day using nothing else. I checked the files before publishing: Compose accepts the configuration, and Nginx accepts the config that is embedded in it.

What each file is for

  • Dockerfile answers one question: what does a machine need to run this PHP code? It produces an image with PHP 8.4, the extensions Laravel uses, and Composer.
  • compose.yaml answers the other: which containers run, and how are they connected? It starts that PHP image three times with different commands, and adds Nginx and MySQL.

You need Docker with Compose 2.23 or newer, because the Nginx config is written inside compose.yaml. Check with docker compose version.

File 1: the Dockerfile

FROM php:8.4-fpm

# System libraries the PHP extensions need, then the extensions themselves
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        git unzip libzip-dev libicu-dev libpng-dev libjpeg62-turbo-dev libfreetype6-dev \
    && docker-php-ext-configure gd --with-freetype --with-jpeg \
    && docker-php-ext-install pdo_mysql zip intl gd exif pcntl bcmath opcache \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Composer, copied from its official image
COPY --from=composer:2 /usr/bin/composer /usr/bin/composer

WORKDIR /var/www

EXPOSE 9000
CMD ["php-fpm"]

What matters here:

  • One RUN for packages and extensions. Installing and cleaning up in the same step keeps the image small, because the package lists never get saved into a layer.
  • The extensions. pdo_mysql for the database, zip and intl for Composer packages and formatting, gd for image handling, pcntl for queue workers, bcmath for money maths, and opcache for speed.
  • Composer is copied, not installed. COPY --from=composer:2 takes the binary straight from the official image.
  • No application code is copied in. The project folder is mounted by Compose instead, so a git pull on the server updates the running code without rebuilding the image.

File 2: compose.yaml

name: myapp

# Shared by every container that runs your PHP code
x-php: &php
  build: .
  restart: unless-stopped
  working_dir: /var/www
  volumes:
    - .:/var/www
  env_file: .env
  environment:
    DB_HOST: db
  depends_on:
    db:
      condition: service_healthy

services:
  # PHP-FPM: runs the application
  app:
    <<: *php

  # Processes queued jobs
  queue:
    <<: *php
    command: php artisan queue:work --tries=3 --max-time=3600

  # Runs scheduled tasks (replaces the cron entry)
  scheduler:
    <<: *php
    command: php artisan schedule:work

  # Nginx: serves files and passes PHP requests to "app"
  web:
    image: nginx:stable-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${APP_PORT:-8080}:80"
    volumes:
      - .:/var/www:ro
    configs:
      - source: nginx
        target: /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
    depends_on:
      - app

  db:
    image: mysql:8.4
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: ${DB_DATABASE}
      MYSQL_USER: ${DB_USERNAME}
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "mysqladmin ping -h 127.0.0.1 -uroot -p$$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

# The Nginx config lives here, so there is no third file to keep track of.
# Every "$" that belongs to Nginx is written "$$" so Compose leaves it alone.
configs:
  nginx:
    content: |
      server {
          listen 80;
          root /var/www/public;
          index index.php;
          client_max_body_size 50M;

          location / {
              try_files $$uri $$uri/ /index.php?$$query_string;
          }

          location ~ \.php$$ {
              fastcgi_pass app:9000;
              fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $$realpath_root$$fastcgi_script_name;
              include fastcgi_params;
          }

          location ~ /\.(?!well-known) {
              deny all;
          }
      }

volumes:
  db-data:

The shared block

x-php: &php defines settings once, and <<: *php reuses them. The app, queue and scheduler services are the same image with the same code and environment. Only the command differs. Change the PHP setup in one place and all three follow.

Waiting for the database

MySQL needs several seconds on first start. condition: service_healthy makes the PHP containers wait until the health check passes, which removes the "Connection refused" error you get when you run migrations too early.

Nginx without a third file

The configs block holds the Nginx server config as text and mounts it into the web container. One rule to remember: Compose treats $ as the start of a variable, so every $ that Nginx should see is written as $$. Inside the container it becomes a normal $uri.

Where the data lives

The database files are in the named volume db-data. Containers can be removed and recreated freely; the volume stays until you delete it on purpose.

The .env values these files read

Compose reads the same .env file Laravel uses. Add one line Laravel does not have by default, the root password:

APP_PORT=8080

DB_CONNECTION=mysql
DB_HOST=db
DB_PORT=3306
DB_DATABASE=laravel
DB_USERNAME=laravel
DB_PASSWORD=choose-a-strong-password
DB_ROOT_PASSWORD=choose-another-strong-password

DB_HOST is db, the service name. Inside the Compose network, containers reach each other by service name, not by localhost. And DB_USERNAME must not be root, because the MySQL image refuses to create a second root user.

First start

# 1. Build the image and start everything
docker compose up -d --build

# 2. Install PHP dependencies and prepare Laravel
docker compose exec app composer install
docker compose exec app php artisan key:generate
docker compose exec app php artisan migrate
docker compose exec app php artisan storage:link

# 3. Build front-end assets with a throwaway Node container
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/app -w /app node:22-alpine sh -c "npm ci && npm run build"

# 4. Let PHP write to the folders it needs
docker compose exec app chown -R www-data:www-data storage bootstrap/cache

Open http://localhost:8080. Node is not part of the PHP image on purpose: you only need it for a few seconds to build assets, so a temporary container does the job and disappears.

Managing everything with these two files

From here on, every routine task is a docker compose command run in the project folder.

TaskCommand
Start the stackdocker compose up -d
Stop it (data is kept)docker compose down
See what is runningdocker compose ps
Follow the logs of one servicedocker compose logs -f app
Run any Artisan commanddocker compose exec app php artisan tinker
Run Composerdocker compose exec app composer require vendor/package
Open a shell in the containerdocker compose exec app bash
Open a MySQL promptdocker compose exec db mysql -u laravel -p laravel
Restart queue workers after a code changedocker compose restart queue
Run three queue workersdocker compose up -d --scale queue=3
Apply a change to .env or compose.yamldocker compose up -d
Rebuild after changing the Dockerfiledocker compose up -d --build

Deploying an update

git pull
docker compose exec app composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/app -w /app node:22-alpine sh -c "npm ci && npm run build"
docker compose exec app php artisan migrate --force
docker compose exec app php artisan optimize
docker compose restart queue scheduler

Put those lines in a deploy.sh script if you like, but the two files above are still the only configuration.

Backing up and restoring the database

# Backup
docker compose exec db sh -c 'exec mysqldump -uroot -p"$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" "$MYSQL_DATABASE"' > backup.sql

# Restore
docker compose exec -T db sh -c 'exec mysql -uroot -p"$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" "$MYSQL_DATABASE"' < backup.sql

Keep backups out of the project folder, or add them to .gitignore. A database dump committed by accident puts customer data and password hashes into your git history.

Changing the setup later

Because everything is in two files, changes are small and easy to review:

  • Need a PHP extension? Add it to the docker-php-ext-install line and run docker compose up -d --build.
  • Need Redis? Add a service with image: redis:7-alpine, set REDIS_HOST: redis in the shared block, and add the redis PHP extension with pecl install redis.
  • Want phpMyAdmin locally? Add a phpmyadmin service with PMA_HOST: db. Do not expose it on a public server.
  • Another port? Change APP_PORT in .env.
  • Bigger uploads? Raise client_max_body_size in the config block, and upload_max_filesize in PHP to match.

Problems you may run into

What you seeCauseFix
A change in .env has no effectContainers read env_file only when they are created.Run docker compose up -d. A plain restart is not enough.
Connection refused to the databaseDB_HOST is 127.0.0.1, or MySQL was still starting.Set DB_HOST=db and wait for docker compose ps to show the database as healthy.
502 Bad GatewayThe app container is not running.Read docker compose logs app.
Permission denied writing logs or cachestorage is not owned by the PHP user.Run the chown command from the first start.
Port is already allocatedSomething else uses the port.Change APP_PORT and run docker compose up -d.
Nginx fails with an "invalid variable" errorA single $ in the config block.Write $$ for every Nginx variable.
Queued jobs still run old codeWorkers keep the code they started with in memory.docker compose restart queue after each deploy.

Before you use this in production

  • Put HTTPS in front of it. A proxy such as Cloudflare, or the reverse proxy in your hosting panel, can forward to APP_PORT.
  • Set APP_ENV=production and APP_DEBUG=false.
  • Do not publish the MySQL port. This file does not, so the database is reachable only from the other containers.
  • Schedule the backup command, and test a restore once.
  • Watch disk space. Run docker system df now and then, and docker builder prune to clear old build cache.

Deploying behind Plesk and Cloudflare on a VPS is covered step by step in Deploying Dockerized Laravel Apps on Hostinger VPS with Plesk & Cloudflare.

Summary

One Dockerfile describes the PHP environment. One compose.yaml describes the containers, the network between them, the Nginx config and the data volume. Everything else, from the first start to deploys and backups, is a docker compose command. A new developer can clone the project, add an .env file, run one command and have the same stack you run in production.

References: Compose file reference and the official PHP image.
